newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP sees Asia metal consumption lift.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP sees Asia metal consumption lift.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), Australia's largest steel producer and the world's number two copper producer, said on Monday it sees a big rise in metal consumption in Asia as developing nations continue to grow.

Asia excluding Japan would account for 45 percent of world steel consumption in about 10 years if Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand consumed the same tonnage of steel per head as south Korea's current level, Robin Stewardson, BHP chief economist, told the Asia-Pacific Commodities Markets conference.
If China consumed only half of South Korea's present steel consumption per head, Asia excluding Japan would consume 60 percent of world steel in 10 years, he added.

"The overall conclusion is that growth in demand in Asia will be very very high in the next decade and will account for very significant and much larger shares of world metal demand," he said. Patterns in steel also would be evident in consumption of copper and other metals, he said.
The China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp estimates China will require 1.3 million tonnes of refined copper by 2000, about 300,000 tonnes more than the domestic supply.

Through its copper mining and processing operations located in the United States, South America and Papua New Guinea, BHP produces about one million tonnes of copper a year, making it the world's second biggest producer behind Chile's Codelco.
